Utility Poles 2D Insight: Norway: wooden poles, usually with a small black metal cap on top. Lamps are held by one thick bolt. Small black pole plates in the south-east, larger black or red ones in Oslo.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Oman: wooden poles with a metal bar carrying three insulators mounted above the top of the post. Two or three poles joined in an X also appear (not in the UAE).
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Oman: white lane lines with a yellow edge line; red-bordered warning triangles.
Pakistan: white lines on main roads; red-bordered warning triangles.
Palestine: white lines; red-bordered warning triangles.
Panama: yellow centre line with solid white edges; yellow diamond warning signs; street names use 'Calle'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Paraguay: rectangular concrete poles with ladder slots from the base to mid-height, often with a white-painted bottom (sometimes the flag) or yellow paint with black text.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Paraguay: yellow diamond warning signs; street names use 'Calle'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Peru: round concrete poles with a pointed (or flat) top, black-and-yellow (or other) markings at the base, black danger signs with a yellow triangle, and concrete H-bars.
Bollards 2D Insight: Peru: rounded plastic post with a yellow top (sometimes a red-and-white reflector instead). Triangular concrete posts with a yellow top or a painted red reflector are common too.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Peru: yellow centre line with solid white edges; yellow diamond warning signs; street names use 'Jirón / Calle'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Philippines: round concrete poles with three insulators on top, single insulators on short brackets, and bright yellow, orange or blue markings that stop above the ground.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Philippines: white lines; yellow diamond warning signs.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Poland: concrete poles with small holes that stop before the ground (Hungary's run all the way).
Bollards 2D Insight: Poland: white wedge post with a red band holding a thin white reflector, so it looks like the Polish flag.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Poland: warning triangles with a yellow background; street names use 'ulica (ul.)'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Portugal: concrete poles with long ladders (France and Spain have short ones).
Bollards 2D Insight: Portugal: white plastic post with a flat top and a slanted black band that starts right at the top, holding a wide white or orange reflector. Spain's reflector is smaller and yellow.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Portugal: white dashed centre line with solid white edges; white warning triangles with a red border; street names use 'Rua'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Puerto Rico: Mexican-style octagonal concrete pole; large square concrete poles too.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Puerto Rico: double yellow centre line with solid white edges; yellow diamond warning signs; street names use 'Calle'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Qatar: round concrete poles with a crossbar of three insulators (the middle one higher) held by two diagonal braces.
Bollards 2D Insight: Qatar: round post with a rounded top, painted black and white, with a yellow rectangular reflector on both sides.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Qatar: white lane lines with a yellow edge line; red-bordered warning triangles.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Réunion: the same concrete poles as mainland France.
Bollards 2D Insight: Réunion: round white post with a domed top and a red reflective band wrapping all the way around.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Réunion: street names use 'Rue'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Romania: concrete poles with medium-sized holes the whole length and a white-painted bottom.

Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Romania: white dashed centre line with solid white edges; white warning triangles with a red border; street names use 'Strada'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Russia: octagonal grey concrete pole held up by a diagonal concrete strut, with a white-painted base.
Bollards 2D Insight: Russia: white post with a diagonal black stripe across the upper half and a small red-white reflector inside it.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Russia: white dashed centre line with solid white edges; white warning triangles with a red border; street names use 'улица (ул.)'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Rwanda: tapering round or square concrete poles; light poles with blue bases on main roads.

San Marino: street names use 'Via'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Senegal: ladder-style concrete poles, like parts of France.
Bollards 2D Insight: Senegal: the French post, a white cylinder with a pointed top and a red or grey band.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Senegal: street names use 'Rue'.

Bollards 2D Insight: Serbia: white post with a black top; the reflector always leans to the left, red on the front and white on the back. Montenegro uses the same post.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Serbia: street names use 'улица / ulica'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Singapore: almost no utility poles; cables run underground.
Bollards 2D Insight: Singapore: no roadside posts; look for yellow kerb lines and zig-zag road markings instead.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Singapore: white lines with single or double yellow kerb lines; zig-zag lines before crossings.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Slovakia: wide round concrete poles, often in pairs, with short metal insulator bars (same as Czechia). Wooden poles are a bit more common than in Czechia. Yellow numbered circles in Nitra and Trnava.
Bollards 2D Insight: Slovakia: same as Czechia, a white (or dark blue) post with two horizontal orange rectangles on the front and one white vertical rectangle on the back.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Slovakia: white dashed centre line with solid white edges; street names use 'ulica'.

Bollards 2D Insight: Slovenia: white post with a black cap (sometimes with a small knob). Red rectangle on the front, grey/white on the back.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Slovenia: white dashed centre line with solid white edges; street names use 'ulica / cesta'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: South Africa: wooden poles with a crossarm, in towns and the countryside alike.
Bollards 2D Insight: South Africa: slim white posts with bright yellow (right) and red (left) reflective strips.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: South Africa: white dashed centre line with solid yellow outer edges; white warning triangles with a red border.

Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: South Korea: double yellow centre line with solid white edges; warning triangles with a yellow background; street names use '로 / 길'.

Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Spain: white dashed centre line with solid white edges; white warning triangles with a red border; street names use 'Calle'.

Bollards 2D Insight: Sri Lanka: white stone post shaped like a truncated pyramid with a black-painted bottom (short or long).
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Sri Lanka: white lines on main roads; street = Mawatha (Sinhala) or Road.
Svalbard: street names use 'veien'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: Sweden: plain round wooden pole with a small yellow number plate nailed at eye level.

Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Sweden: white dashed centre line with dashed white outer edges; warning triangles with a yellow background; street names use 'gatan / vägen'.

Utility Poles 2D Insight: United Kingdom: wooden poles with thin metal climbing rods, small round ID discs (Ireland's are rectangles), tall white/yellow tags with letters and digits, and yellow 'Danger of Death' stickers.

Examples: Washington, a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front and two small squares on the back; Montana and South Dakota, a white diamond on top; Oregon, a long white rectangle; Wisconsin, white posts with black reflectors; Colorado and Wyoming, a dark metal post with a round white reflector just below the top.
Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: United States: double yellow centre line with solid white edges; yellow diamond warning signs.
U.S. Virgin Islands: yellow diamond warning signs.

Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Uruguay: yellow diamond warning signs; street names use 'Calle'.

Road Lines & Signs 2D Insight: Vietnam: white lines; yellow warning triangles with a red border.
